sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Nov 17 at 7,340.53, its lowest close of the past month and 5.4% under the Oct 21 high. The Nasdaq 100 is at 27,001.78, 9.5% below that same Oct 21 peak and near the bottom of its 1-month range. Euro Stoxx 50 is mid-range, up 1.1% over the month. VIX closed at 25.46, up from 18.44 a month earlier. The week itself is light: 15 scheduled reports across the S&P 500, Russell 1000 and core names, concentrated in technology (6), with consumer-cyclical and industrials at 3 each. All 15 dates are still estimates.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon Nov 23: HPE and Zoom report into technology, where the 3-day median reaction off recent prints is +0.3% across 769 names. Tue Nov 24 is the busiest day: Analog Devices, HP Inc, Workday and Nutanix (technology), plus Best Buy, Burlington and Dick's (consumer-cyclical, median +0.4%) and Dollar Tree (consumer-defensive, median -0.3%). Wed Nov 25: Deere reports into industrials, median +0.3%. None of these 15 sit in the sectors with the largest recent moves (mining, copper, energy), so this week's prints are a separate read from those clusters.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: The largest recent median reactions are mining (+4.6% across 215 tickers, 2,766 news items), copper (-2.5%, 6 tickers, 231 items) and energy (+1.7%, 315 tickers, 5,130 items). Energy's news window is thick at over 1,000 items. Mining and copper are weaker bases: copper rests on only 6 tickers. None of the three has a scheduled reporter this week, so they offer context rather than a read-through to the week's prints.
